result.summary: The image shows a residential urban intersection with basic pedestrian infrastructure including sidewalks and a marked crosswalk. However, the building's proximity to the corner creates a significant visual obstruction for both drivers and pedestrians, and there is a lack of dedicated pedestrian signals.

hazards.name: Blind Corner
hazards.description: The brick building is situated directly at the property line at the intersection, severely limiting sightlines between pedestrians and approaching vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Center-left, where the building meets the sidewalk corner

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signalization
hazards.description: While a traffic light is present for vehicles, no dedicated pedestrian signal head is visible to guide safe crossing intervals.
hazards.location_in_image: Traffic light pole in the foreground

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and move pedestrians into the driver's line of sight before they enter the roadway.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Replace the standard transverse markings with continental or ladder-style markings to increase visibility to approaching motorists.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear information on remaining crossing time.

result.summary: The intersection features a high-visibility continental crosswalk and a well-maintained sidewalk with a curb ramp. However, the environment lacks visible pedestrian-specific signals and a median refuge, increasing exposure time for those crossing the multi-lane roadway.

hazards.name: Missing Pedestrian Signal
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal head is visible, requiring pedestrians to interpret vehicle signals which may not provide sufficient clearance intervals.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the intersection near the traffic light pole.

hazards.name: Unprotected Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The width of the roadway increases pedestrian exposure to traffic without a mid-crossing refuge island.
hazards.location_in_image: Spanning the width of the roadway at the crosswalk.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear information on remaining crossing time.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct curb extensions to shorten the crossing distance and increase the visibility of pedestrians waiting to cross.

result.summary: The image depicts a two-lane urban roadway with a paved sidewalk and street trees on the left side. A signalized intersection is visible in the distance with a marked crosswalk, though it lacks visible pedestrian-specific signals or curb extensions to reduce crossing exposure.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No visible pedestrian signal heads at the signalized intersection, which may lead to confusion about when it is safe to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: At the intersection in the background

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide roadway at the intersection increases pedestrian exposure to traffic without any refuge or narrowing.
hazards.location_in_image: Intersection area where the white van is stopped

interventions.title: Install Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Add dedicated pedestrian signals with countdown timers to provide clear crossing information and improve safety.

result.summary: The intersection provides basic pedestrian infrastructure including traffic signals, marked crosswalks, and curb ramps. However, the environment is constrained by narrow sidewalks, utility poles located within the pedestrian path, and degraded pavement surfaces.

hazards.name: Sightline obstruction from parked vehicles
hazards.description: Vehicles parked very close to the crosswalk may obscure pedestrians from the view of approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the intersection along the curb

hazards.name: Utility pole obstruction
hazards.description: A large utility pole is situated directly on the sidewalk corner, narrowing the accessible path for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Degraded pavement
hazards.description: Cracking and uneven pavement surfaces within the intersection and crosswalk area.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and prevent illegal parking near the corner.

interventions.title: Pavement Rehabilitation
interventions.description: Repair cracks and resurface the intersection to provide a smoother and safer crossing surface.
